title: compactify presubmit tooling and introduce dependency staging + micro-toolchain images
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: CI presubmit setup has grown organically and causes high setup latency and flakiness across macOS/Linux/Windows runners. This PR compacts the presubmit tooling into a single orchestrator, replaces heavyweight toolchain images with small micro-toolchain images focused on language runtimes, and adds a dependency staging step to reduce transient npm/pip/go module failures in CI.

What this PR does (high level): squash commits by intent and split into 3 themes: 1) presubmit orchestrator - a Go-based controller that routes lint/test jobs to language-specific shards and reuses an immutable cache key; 2) micro-toolchains - new docker images under ci/toolchain/ that contain only runtime+pkg manager bits (smaller layers, faster pulls); 3) dependency staging - a lightweight step that warms registries and vendors flaky transitive deps into a short-lived registry mirror when upstream fails.

Why it matters: average presubmit setup time dropped ~38% in our internal sample jobs; observed a ~60% reduction in transient dependency failures on nightly and PR runs during the stabilisation window. This reduces developer wait time and the number of noisy reruns.

Checklist: - [x] Implement presubmit orchestrator binary (cmd/presubmit) - [x] Add micro-toolchain Dockerfiles and build matrix - [x] Add dependency staging layer (scripts/ci/stage-deps.sh) - [x] Migrate key workflows to use concurrency groups and cache scope - [x] Update documentation (docs/ci-presubmit.md) - [x] Smoke tests + e2e presubmit run on canary repo

Testing and validation: multiple runs against redwood-examples and core repo: - unit tests for orchestrator (go test ./cmd/presubmit -> pass) - integration smoke (presubmit canary with 12 PRs) - nightly run for 3 days showed stable cache warming and mirror fallbacks. CI matrices passed. See ci_checks for granular results.

Rollout plan: initial rollout was gated behind a feature flag (repo-level) and staged to non-critical repos for 48h. After metrics stabilized rollout was expanded to the monorepo presubmit default. Backout: revert the workflow YAML and stop using the new orchestrator; old scripts are preserved under scripts/presubmit/legacy for emergency fallback.

Notes and follow-ups: - We'll follow up with a separate PR to add granular observability (per-language presubmit latencies and cache hit rates) - Need to coordinate with Platform SRE to publish micro-toolchain images to our internal registry and lifecycle policy.

Commits summary: 1) add presubmit orchestrator + README 2) add micro-toolchain Dockerfiles and make targets 3) add dependency staging script + registry mirror config 4) migrate .github/workflows/presubmit.yml to call orchestrator 5) docs and tests

Changed areas (high level): .github/workflows/presubmit.yml, ci/toolchain/Dockerfile.node-micro, ci/toolchain/Dockerfile.go-micro, cmd/presubmit/main.go, scripts/ci/stage-deps.sh, scripts/presubmit/legacy/*, docs/ci-presubmit.md, Makefile (ci targets), go.mod, package-lock.json

Related work: ENG-4215 (presubmit reduction), ENG-4300 (ci reliability), SUP-1287 (support incident that motivated dependency staging).

review_comments: Evan Miller: Overall strong. Two requests: (1) add a health endpoint to the orchestrator so SRE can probe; (2) restrict the mirror to a whitelist of packages to avoid accidental staleness. See inline comments.
Author (Aisha Patel): addressed both. health endpoint added at /healthz and mirror whitelist is configurable via CI env var. Also added smoke tests for mirror behavior.
Priya Sharma: Please add telemetry tags for repo and language shard. Also let's gate the micro-toolchain publish until registry retention policy is agreed.
Author: Added telemetry tags and feature-flagged registry publish. Noted next steps in follow-ups.
Liam O'Connor: CI cache keying looks good. Suggest we run one more full presubmit night on the monorepo before fully flipping the flag. Approved after the extra nightly run passed.
release_notes: Compact presubmit orchestrator and micro-toolchain images reduce CI setup time and transient dependency failures; added dependency staging to reduce flaky upstream registry failures. No user-facing product changes.
notes_for_ops: Publish ci/toolchain images to internal registry: registry.redwood-ci/redwood/toolchain:node-micro-v1 and :go-micro-v1. Ensure retention policy >7d for stabilisation window. SRE to add an alert for orchestrator healthz failing >2m.
